item.title: Five Wilderness Bound Features: Mojang details camping-focused update; autumn aesthetic and builds
item.description: Mojang's Wilderness Bound update will bring players to a new autumn biome. This update introduces abandoned camps and valuable loot for explorers. Straw beds will allow players to skip nights without changing their spawn point. New furniture, including cushions, will enhance building and roleplaying experiences. Concrete and wool stairs and slabs will offer more architectural options.

item.title: China tested nanobubbles across a 3,300-square-metre section of Taihu Lake; within 20 days...
item.description: Innovative nanobubble technology has significantly diminished toxic cyanobacteria in Taihu Lake, achieving an impressive ninety percent decrease in chlorophyll-a levels during the testing phase. By integrating cavitation with ozone nanobubbles, this method not only enhances water quality but also elevates dissolved oxygen levels, presenting a hopeful solution for extensive ecological restoration.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Meet Callum Smith: The armless racer, 23, steering with his feet and chasing a historic Le Mans debut
item.description: Callum Smith, 23, was born without arms but is now pursuing a racing career by steering with his feet. Having crossed 110mph on track, he has joined Team BRIT and is working towards his racing licence. Alongside quadruple amputee Harvey Phillips, Smith hopes to help the team achieve its historic Le Mans ambition.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2023, Australia put a 330-square-metre floating wetland on a wastewater lagoon
item.description: Over the course of two years, research revealed that floating wetlands successfully diminished methane emissions by sixty-six percent, alongside notable reductions in carbon dioxide and nitrous oxide levels. The native vegetation on these platforms is crucial in nurturing beneficial microbes that tackle pollutants and gases effectively. This eco-friendly treatment method reveals a significant advancement in wastewater management, with ongoing tests on analogous floating wetlands in regional agricultural dams.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Celia Hunter flew a war-surplus plane to Alaska in 1947 and built a wilderness life near Denali
item.description: Celia Hunter dedicated her life to protecting Alaska's wild landscapes. She co-founded conservation groups and championed public land protection for decades. Hunter's efforts helped preserve over 100 million acres of Alaskan wilderness. She continued her advocacy until her final moments, writing letters to politicians. Her lifelong commitment significantly impacted environmental conservation in Alaska.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2021, a North Yorkshire estate began restoring 2,500 acres of farmed land; four years later...
item.description: After four years dedicated to rewilding, Broughton Sanctuary has successfully documented over 1,700 species. The estate boasts more than 330,000 trees planted, significantly enhancing forest cover. By managing livestock and beavers, diverse habitats are flourishing. Extensive fencing removal has further facilitated wildlife movement. Going forward, plans include reintroducing native species and expanding vibrant wetland areas for richer biodiversity.

item.description: Founded in 1918, a family-owned business in Indiana proudly celebrates over a century of service. Remarkably, it boasts a highly dedicated workforce, with several employees retiring after forty to fifty years. The company has successfully navigated industry shifts while staying true to its original operational methods, fostering strong customer loyalty and benefiting from the expertise of its long-serving employees.

item.title: England released beavers into a Dorset woodland in 2025; one year later, their dams had...
item.description: Beavers newly introduced in Dorset have remarkably transformed a woodland area into a flourishing wetland. Through their natural dam-building, these creatures have slowed down water movement, resulting in the formation of deep pools. This ecological shift has rejuvenated the local fauna, reintroducing various native species to the Purbeck region. Additionally, the beaver dams serve to mitigate flooding on nearby roads during heavy rains, highlighting nature’s essential contribution to environmental resilience.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Make AI-merica Great Again: Meme Lord Trump’s digital feed goes off rails again
item.description: Donald Trump posted numerous AI-generated images on Truth Social over the weekend. These images ranged from self-congratulatory to geopolitically consequential, causing confusion. The posts included depictions of historical figures and geopolitical scenarios, raising alarm. Critics worry about the distinction between memes and actual policy signals from the president. Concerns about cognitive decline and national security implications are being voiced by analysts.

item.title: San Antonio girls’ flag football team sees huge growth
item.description: In San Antonio, girls are seizing the chance to excel in flag football, with the Alamo City Lady Roadrunners witnessing impressive growth from its inception. This emerging sport is paving the way for college scholarships and promising career paths. With flag football slated for the Olympics, aspiring athletes are presented with exciting new opportunities. The program aims to cultivate local competition to enhance player development.
